proposed.explanation: Your friend's claim is inaccurate. Telecom Egypt recorded a net profit of 22,578,063,000 EGP in 2025, up from 10,111,328,000 EGP in 2024, which is a growth of approximately 123%, not over ten-fold. Your friend appears to have confused net profit with total assets, which reached 225,882,527,000 EGP at year-end 2025. Company fundamentals show solid expansion, with operating revenues rising from 81,677,812,000 EGP in 2024 to 106,672,946,000 EGP in 2025, and basic/diluted earnings per share increasing from 4.79 EGP to 11.93 EGP. Given your 5-year horizon for retirement savings and existing emergency fund, buying 352 shares at 141.95 EGP per share requires 49,966.40 EGP, within your 50,000.00 EGP available cash. However, allocating all cash to ETEL increases single-stock concentration risk significantly, which medium risk tolerance investors should keep in mind.

This represents a strong increase from the 2024 net profit of 10,111,328,000 EGP.
Your friend likely confused net profit with total assets, which stood at 225,882,527,000 EGP in 2025.
Operating revenues grew to 106,672,946,000 EGP in 2025.
This compares to operating revenues of 81,677,812,000 EGP in 2024.
Earnings per share increased to 11.93 EGP in 2025.
Earnings per share was 4.79 EGP in 2024.

limitations: Putting all remaining cash into ETEL creates high portfolio concentration risk in a single company.
Historical financial performance does not guarantee future earnings or share price performance.
